newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German shares hit fresh record, dlr strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German shares hit fresh record, dlr strong.

text.p: German shares powered to fresh trading highs on Monday, building on last week's strength with the aid of a strong dollar and buoyant Wall Street.
Europe's other major bourses opened weak, with London undercut by a number of major stocks going ex-dividend and Paris consolidating as investors cashed on last week's big gains.
The dollar hit a six-week high against the mark but later slipped a little after France and Germany reiterated at the weekend their commitment to a stable franc-mark rate.

German government bonds, or bunds, succumbed to modest profit-taking early one, while British gilt futures slipped a little before steadying after economic data showing manufacturing had expanded for the sixth straight month.
The London copper market began its trading month in a nervous mood with the possibility of turmoil on Wednesday when December options expire.
Traders said that if all investors with open call options elected to take delivery of the metal, their demands could exceed the amount of copper held in the warehouses of the London Metal Exchange.
"The only thing you can say is that it will be a bumpy ride with lots of volatility," one senior trader said.
On European equity markets, Germany started the week in a starring role, with the 30-share DAX index opening floor trade at a fresh record.
Building on last week's rally, the index hit a trading record of 2,860.24 points before slipping a few points in relatively thin trade.
Carmaker Volkswagen slipped 11.5 marks in early trade to 604 marks on speculation about its legal battle with General Motors over accusations of industrial espionage against the German company.
British shares were marked cautiously lower at the start of trading, depressed by a batch of stocks going ex-dividend and continuing fears of a rise in interest rates.
The FTSE 100 index was down 6.8 points at 4,051 by 1015 GMT but off its lows.

Traders said the market could find support from Wall Street's performance on Friday when the Dow rose 22 points but was likely to be weighed down by the continued strength of sterling and worries over interest rates.
They said there were fears the next British monetary policy meeting on December 11 could see a rise in interest rates.

"Sterling has had a rip-roaring time and it is beginning to hurt the exporters," said one trader. "And with rising house prices, if I was a Bank of England official I would be pressing the need for a rate increase quite quickly."
French shares staged an orderly retreat at the opening, with modest profit-taking after last week's substantial gains.
The market is likely consolidate around the psychologically-important 2,300 level before attacking the previous historic high at 2,360.98, traders said.
"The market's got a good feel to it," said one broker.
The dollar drifted off a fresh six week high at 1.5423 marks in early trade but remained just above 1.54 after France stuck to its franc fort policy but reiterated a desire for a stronger dollar.

"The prospects for giving up the franc fort policy or loosening it are very slim. We are now very close to monetary union and giving up on the franc fort would complicate the transition to EMU and perhaps jeopardise the achievement of EMU in 1999," said Norman Williams, European economist at BZW.
French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl reaffirmed at the weekend their commitment to a stable franc-mark exchange rate.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.71 yen and 1.5401 marks against 113.90 yen and 1.5320 marks in late Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 6.8 points at 4,051.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 3.38 points at 2,312.28.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 11.2 points at 2,856.72.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $370.50 against $371.30 previously. Silver was down one cent at $4.72. Platinum was down $0.50 cents at $374.0.
